messages.content: You can call send_email to compose and send messages. Always confirm critical fields before sending.
Send an email to alice@example.com thanking her for yesterday's meeting and proposing a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM.

message.content:
<think>The user wants me to send an email to alice@example.com. I have all the information needed:
- To: alice@example.com
- Subject: Should be about the meeting follow-up
- Body: Thank her for yesterday's meeting and propose a follow-up call on Friday at 3 PM

I should compose a professional email with these elements. Let me use the send_email function.
</think>


<minimax:tool_call>
<invoke name="send_email">
<parameter name="to">["alice@example.com"]</parameter>
<parameter name="subject">Follow-up from Yesterday's Meeting</parameter>
<parameter name="body">Hi Alice,

Thank you for taking the time to meet with me yesterday. I really appreciated the discussion and found your insights valuable.

I would like to schedule a follow-up call to continue our conversation. Would Friday at 3 PM work for you?

Please let me know if that time is convenient or if you'd prefer an alternative.

Best regards</parameter>
</invoke>
</minimax:tool_call>
